name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Require every PR to include a ticket link in the title or description.

This forces engineers to connect code changes to business value, making it easier to track impact and justify work. The trade-off is a slight increase in PR review friction, but the long-term payoff in transparency and accountability outweighs the cost.

name: Scriv
text: Mandatory ticket links in every PR create a new bottleneck—teams will waste time hunting for tickets or inventing placeholder Jira IDs just to merge. Instead, enforce ticket links only on merged PRs, where the real risk of orphaned work matters. That settles it: link coverage still climbs, but without slowing down the flow.

name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Require every merged PR to include a ticket link in the commit message or PR body, not during review.

This forces engineers to connect code changes to business value *after* the work is done, ensuring no orphaned changes slip through. The trade-off is a small uptick in post-merge cleanup if tickets are missing, but it avoids review friction and keeps the focus on shipping. Link coverage climbs without slowing down the pipeline.

name: Sift
text: The real risk is that post-merge enforcement turns ticket links into an afterthought—engineers will slap in any old ticket to clear the gate, not to track impact. A better alternative: require ticket links *before* review, but only enforce them on merged PRs, splitting the difference. That settles it: we get the tracking without the bottleneck.

name: Scope
text:
**Decision:** Require ticket links in PR titles or descriptions *before* review, but enforce them strictly only at merge time.

This forces engineers to connect work to business value upfront, reducing orphaned changes without creating a post-merge scramble. The trade-off is minor PR friction—teams may need to adjust tickets or descriptions—but it’s outweighed by the clarity gained.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Mandatory pre-review ticket links still let engineers game the system—teams will paste dead ticket IDs just to pass the gate, not to track real impact. Instead, require a *live* ticket link that must resolve to an active issue at merge time, not just any string. That settles it: no fake compliance, real coverage.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Require every PR to include a live ticket link in the title or description *before review*, and enforce it strictly at merge time by verifying the link resolves to an active issue.

Result: Link coverage climbs toward 100% without fake IDs or post-merge scramble. Owner: Scriv (analysis-checker).
